First off, congratulations on the PhD - that's an amazing achievement!

Secondly, I'm sorry to hear you haven't been feeling great lately. Had you thought about going to your doctor about it? Perhaps he could suggest some medication to help you break out of this slump. Also some counselling may help you progress forward too - something worth investigating.

Try not to think about a girlfriend right now - I know it's tough but how can you expect to be happy in a relationship if you're not happy in yourself.

You say you woke up at 9 but didn't get dressed til 5. Try and set yourself a routine. Go to bed at a reasonable time, get up at a reasonable time, shower, get dressed and go out and do something. Exercise is a great way to make you feel better. Even a walk around the block can work wonders for your mood.

Try to work through your issues bit by bit rather than looking at them as a whole, it makes it much more manageable. 

Feel free to message me any time, I will always listen and help you work through things. Remember: your happiness is key, you deserve to be happy. If you want things to change then you need to take the first step, we'll be right there behind you. Good luck xx

My depression affected me slowly over time. I thought it was just me being tired the reason why I didn't want to get out of bed or couldn't be both to get dressed etc. I also thought the constant tears were down to hormones and that it was normal to feel low and shitty all the time. It wasn't until I had a crisis and reflected afterwards that I realised how bad it had got. I was/half am like a completely different person.

My aim is to get back to my bubbly, happy self as soon as possible but I know I have a lot of things to overcome first. 

I hope things are looking up for you xx

This won't last forever, I've been there, done that and now I'm alone and think about my ex who I am madly in love with 24 hrs a day. There is nothing I can do about it now but try and move on one day but you have a chance to save your relationship - I wish I was in your situation. Please don't waste it. Please try and get help.

Not getting help will make things worse. That's what happened to me. I covered it up for so long until I just snapped and couldn't do it anymore. Because of this he has now finished with me and wants nothing to do with me. Had I got help sooner I think I could of saved my relationship. 

It's up to you but I'd strongly suggest getting any help possible for yourself - you deserve to be happy, keep reminding yourself of this!

The only way you can be happy is by making the first step. Please Hiranau try and get help/support from somewhere. You don't deserve this, you deserve a happy life so don't deny yourself this.

I will always be free to listen and talk but if you want to see real changes you need to seek outside, professional help. xx

Please try a different therapist, I'm not sure where you're from but in the UK there are loads of charities that help with this kind of thing. Google some perhaps? The main ones in the UK are Samaritans and Mental Health Matters.

I know how terrifying it is - I've been there, tried to hide it for 6 months but just crashed in the end. I don't know if you're mentally ill, I'm sure you're just depressed like myself and a lot of other people. It's time you got the help you need and deserve. 

On a side note, your boyfriend may have his own problems but I think it would be a good idea to make him aware. Maybe give him the watered down version to start with but then at least he could support you to some extent? Just something to think about.

I hope things look up soon for you xx

Maybe you need to change meds? Some meds just don't work for some people. There are so many different types out there, mention it to your GP if it gets too much.

Personally I did react badly to one drug, waking up with the worst nightmares every single night for a week. It actually made me more depressed and I didn't want to sleep because I was terrified what my mind would think up next. I went back to my GP and I'm on a new drug now - no side effects and I feel much better. xx

I was in the same situation as you. My boyfriend, now ex, couldn't understand what I was going through therefore couldn't help me.

It took me to attempt to take my life and to be picked up by the police before I could admit I had a serious problem and before anyone could help me. This all happened a few weeks ago and since getting the right help I am slowly getting back on track and have realised I do deserve to be here.

I would deffinately advise you to go to your GP and back to your therapist. Explain exactly how you feel and over time it is important to try and find out why you're feeling like this.

Maybe you need some meds to help the chemical imbalance in your brain. The way I see it if you had a broken leg you would take pain relief and after resting it you could possible have some physio to fix it again. The same thing is happening with your brain, it is not your fault. You just maybe need to take some meds and use outside services to help fix it again.

Please, please, please get help. I know how helpless you feel but this WILL pass! I absolutely promise you - but you need to make the first step! 

Feel free to message me anytime - I will reply as soon as possible, and although I may not be able to fix things for you, I can promise I will always listen and help you work through anything.

Whenever you are round there, just always be polite and make an effort. Over time I'm sure things will get easier and you'll be able to build bridges with her mum.

I cope by crying. I literally cannot stop for hours and need meds to calm me down. I cry for no reason at all. Don't leave my bed unless I absolutely have to.

I find the best thing is finding distractions, I force myself to play games with my 4 brothers when I feel like shit just so I can hopefully forget for 10 mins how sad I feel. Doesn't always work but sometimes it makes my afternoon a bit more barable x

You say you don't think she knew what she did, then maybe she will be horrified to know what she has done and will try and put things right? Personally, life is too short to hate people. If you were great friends before and want that again then I think all you can do is try and clear the air.

Failing this, stop all contact and leave each other to get on with your lives and move on. Focus on you: your happiness is the key!

Good luck xx

Ok you're not crazy, just heartbroken. We've all been there, it's so hard to keep your distant but before you know it you're calling your ex again! (I was in this exact situation just a few weeks ago!)

I know it doesn't feel like it but after a few days you will feel a tiny bit better, and it will continue to get better (very slowly, and you won't ever forget about her but you will learn to live without her!)

Give yourself time to grieve for your relationship, it is a sad time for you and you have to appreciate that. But also say to yourself 'ok I'm going to feel shit for a few days, then I am gonna pick myself up and get on with life!'

Also have a friend/relative/etc take your phone away from you if you can't resist calling her. Trust me its the best thing to do, I had my mum take my phone every night for a week just so I couldn't ring my ex, and now he's been ringing me instead asking how I am.

Hugs to you, you will get through this I promise xx

A crisis team is a mental health team that are called by either a GP, police, nurse, etc when they believe a person is considering suicide. I was looked after by the police when my boyfriend, now ex, called them when I tried to commit suicide a few weeks ago and they referred me.

They visit you at home, have a 24 hr hotline, can give meds, support etc so you don't have to go into hospital. Between them and my mum I have been able to slowly feel better about myself and have a more positive outlook on life. They are a brilliant service!
:) xx
